heroHeadline: US, Canada Join Philippines in Condemning China Coast Guard Ramming as Beijing Rejects Blame, Doubles Down
heroSubtitle: The diplomatic fallout from the September 18 China Coast Guard ramming of the BFAR vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat off Palawan widened through September 19-20, 2026. The DFA formally condemned the CCG's 'illegal, coercive, aggressive and dangerous' acts as violations of UNCLOS, the 2016 Arbitral Award, COLREGS and SOLAS; US Ambassador Lee Lipton called it a 'deliberate ramming' and Canada issued its own condemnation. China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun and CCG spokesperson Jiang Lue rejected the account, saying the Philippine vessel deliberately cut across the CCG cutter's bow near Xianbin Jiao (Sabina Shoal) and bears responsibility, while reasserting Chinese sovereignty claims. Security analysts warned the growing pattern of close CCG encounters with Philippine civilian vessels could increasingly threaten routine fishery and humanitarian missions. The incident came a day after the same BFAR vessel was refloated following a self-inflicted grounding at Hasa-Hasa (Half Moon) Shoal on September 17, and follows the AFP's September 15 assessment that the Haiyang Dizhi Shihao survey vessel's ~28-day presence off Bajo de Masinloc showed no confirmed drilling activity, amid a weekly tally of 48 Chinese vessels across four contested WPS features.
